title: In a Noetherian ring the zerodivisors are the union of the associated primes
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Call a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset R$ an *associated prime* of $R$ if $\mathfrak q=\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\{a\in R: az=0\}$ for some $z\in R$, and write $\operatorname{Ass}(R)$ for the set of these. Call $x\in R$ a *zerodivisor* if $xy=0$ for some $y\in R$, $y\neq0$, and a *nonzerodivisor* otherwise. Then the set of zerodivisors of $R$ equals $\bigcup_{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}(R)}\mathfrak q$. In particular an element of $R$ lying in no associated prime of $R$ is a nonzerodivisor.
